themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints spiked to 7 THIS WEEK versus a baseline average of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 5500% increase—suggesting either a sudden enforcement crackdown, illegal vendor proliferation, or both in Central Harlem.
evidence: 7 vendor enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 20.79)
No recent local news coverage or community board discussion of vendor issues on record
reporting_angles: Is the city launching a new enforcement operation against street vendors in Central Harlem? Interview DOC or local precinct.
Are illegal vendors clustering in specific neighborhoods (125th Street, major transit hubs)? Map the complaints geographically.

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints reached 6 THIS WEEK compared to 0.1 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 4700% spike—indicating rapid deterioration in public space maintenance or a coordinated posting campaign in Central Harlem.
evidence: 6 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 17.76)
Coincides with graffiti spike last week (8 complaints vs. 0.5 average)
reporting_angles: What is being posted illegally? Interview sanitation workers and community members.
Is this related to the graffiti spike last week—coordinated defacement campaign?

themes_detail.label: Street Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints hit 51 LAST WEEK versus 7.2 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 603% spike—suggesting rapid pavement degradation, pothole formation, or neglected sidewalk maintenance across Central Harlem.
evidence: 51 street condition complaints LAST WEEK vs. 7.2 weekly average (z-score: 6.19)
603% increase coincides with illegal parking spike (134 complaints vs. 74 average)
DOB shows 462 total permit filings in last 90 days with 391 alterations—possible construction-related damage
reporting_angles: Walk major thoroughfares (125th Street, Frederick Douglass Boulevard, Amsterdam Ave) and document pothole/sidewalk conditions.
Is construction activity from 462 recent DOB permits contributing to street damage? Interview DOB and contractors.

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Resurgence
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints reached 8 LAST WEEK versus 0.5 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 1500% spike—indicating either gang activity, coordinated vandalism, or systemic removal failure in Central Harlem.
evidence: 8 graffiti complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 7.5)
Clusters with illegal posting spike this week (6 complaints), suggesting coordinated public space vandalism
reporting_angles: Where is graffiti concentrated geographically? Interview Parks Dept on removal capacity and response time.
Are tags associated with crews or gangs? Speak with local precinct community affairs.

themes_detail.label: Illegal Parking Spike
themes_detail.summary: Illegal parking complaints jumped to 134 LAST WEEK from 74 weekly average—an 81% increase—coinciding with street condition deterioration and suggesting congestion or enforcement gaps in Central Harlem.
evidence: 134 illegal parking complaints LAST WEEK vs. 74 weekly average (z-score: 5.63)
81% increase; also highest-volume complaint category overall at 1,133 complaints over 90 days
Aligns with street condition spike, suggesting blocked access or congestion in same timeframe
reporting_angles: Which streets or blocks have the worst illegal parking? Map complaints by location.
Is enforcement insufficient? Interview NYPD traffic enforcement on staffing and patrol patterns.
